title: Fred Beckett's plunger-mute melody playing
summary: Hampton featured Beckett playing straight melody with a plunger mute into the microphone before a Ruby Blakely vocal, a style Cobb likens to Johnny Hodges.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: But did Hamp feature him much or not?
Fred Beckett played a solo before Ruby Blake come out and sing this tune titled Nightingale. You remember the thing?

And he put a (inaudible) and take a rubber plunger and play nothing but straight melody. Wa-wa-wa-wa-wa-wa-wa-wa-wa-wa-wa, and make chills go up and down your spine, just no nothing but melody, just improvising. But

he had that much soul. He was a soulful man, and not too many people could take a melody other than a Johnny Hudges, and Johnny Hodges was known for this. And his tone, Fred Beckett was the same thing (inaudible).
And got in the microphone. We're at the Strand Theater.
And take the wa-wa with the mute on the inside of that microphone, and I'm telling you it just makes you bloom.
